how-to-take-good-meeting-notes.0: Learning how to take good meeting notes is less about writing faster and more about writing less. The best note-takers do not capture everything. They capture just 3 things people will need later: what was decided, who will do what, and what is still unresolved.
how-to-take-good-meeting-notes.1: Inside: a simple method, 4 formats to choose from, shorthand that speeds you up, and practical answers to the questions people ask most, from Teams meetings to who should take notes.
how-to-take-good-meeting-notes.2: The best way to take meeting notes is the decision-and-action method: ignore most of the discussion and record only decisions, action items with an owner and due date, and open questions. Everything else? Optional.
how-to-take-good-meeting-notes.3: Why does it work? Most people read meeting notes for 1 reason: to find out what they need to do.
how-to-take-good-meeting-notes.4: Meeting notes turn a conversation into a record people can act on. Without them, attendees leave with different memories of the same meeting, and absent colleagues have nothing to go on. Good notes do 4 jobs:
how-to-take-good-meeting-notes.6: Spend 5 minutes before the meeting setting up your notes, because that small step cuts cleanup time afterward: copy a template, paste in the agenda, and add the attendee list. Then you just fill in blanks.
how-to-take-good-meeting-notes.9: During the meeting, write in short fragments under each agenda heading and mark every line with a type. Listen for 3 trigger phrases. "We agreed" signals a decision, "can you" or "I will" marks an action, and "we still need to figure out" flags an open question.
how-to-take-good-meeting-notes.11: No owner or date on an action? Ask before moving on: "Who owns that, and by when?" That one question improves notes more than any tool.
how-to-take-good-meeting-notes.12: After the meeting, spend 10 minutes turning fragments into clear notes, then share them within an hour. Wait until the next day and far fewer people read them. They have moved on.
how-to-take-good-meeting-notes.14: Pick a format to suit the meeting type. Almost every work meeting fits 1 of these 4:
how-to-take-good-meeting-notes.15: Action-focused wins for most business meetings. It matches what readers need.
how-to-take-good-meeting-notes.17: It works well for people who attend many meetings and mainly need to know what they personally must do, and a 2-by-2 table in Word, Google Docs or a notebook is all it takes. Long discussions where context matters? Less useful there, since the Cornell or outline format works better.
how-to-take-good-meeting-notes.19: Five lines. That covers everything someone who missed the meeting needs: 2 decisions, 2 actions and 1 open question, each with a name.
how-to-take-good-meeting-notes.21: Whichever you use, check names, numbers and owners before sharing. AI is fast at structure. Details people act on? That is where it is weakest.
how-to-take-good-meeting-notes.28: The person taking notes should not be the person running the meeting, since facilitating and writing at the same time means both get done badly. Rotate the role. That way it does not always fall to the same person.
how-to-take-good-meeting-notes.30: Be careful not to always assign notes to the most junior person or to the same people by habit. Note-taking is real work. Share it.
how-to-take-good-meeting-notes.33: Record only decisions, action items with an owner and due date, and open questions. Use a template prepared before the meeting and share clean notes within an hour. Mark lines with shorthand such as D: for decision and A: for action. Rewriting them into clean notes afterward is then quick.
how-to-take-good-meeting-notes.36: Ask a colleague to take notes, use shared notes in Teams or Google Docs, or use an AI note taker so you can focus on the conversation. Agree on 1 note-taker before the meeting starts. Otherwise 3 people may take partial notes that nobody combines afterward.
